causebase_summary: The Aboriginal Legal Rights Movement (ALRM) is an Aboriginal community-controlled legal service based in Adelaide on Kaurna country that works across South Australia. ALRM pursues social justice, equality and wellbeing for Aboriginal people of South Australia, with particular focus on those detained in police custody or imprisoned. It operates a Custody Notification Service and provides criminal court services and programs for Aboriginal people across the state. ALRM also offers a Confirmation of Aboriginality service, membership and volunteering opportunities, and runs public programming such as Law Week panels. The organisation issues media releases and advocacy statements, invites applications for Aboriginal community board members and accepts tax-deductible donations to support its work.

causebase_summary: South Australian Rainbow Advocacy Alliance Inc. (SARAA) is a South Australia‑based peak body that advocates for LGBTIQA+ people across the state. As of the cited sources it runs policy advocacy and submissions (for example on births, deaths and marriages regulations), correspondence with health authorities about gender‑affirming care, and public events and commemorations such as Trans Day of Visibility and youth forums. causebase_summary: Banks Street Newmarket Community Preschooling Centre Inc (Banks Street Kindy) is a not-for-profit community kindergarten operating on the grounds of Newmarket State School in Newmarket, Queensland. As of 2026 it runs community kindergarten sessions with daily outdoor play and nature-based programming, including regular Bush Kindy visits to nearby Banks Street Reserve. The kindergarten runs an arts program and an annual art show, maintains gardens and chickens, and organises family-facing events. A volunteer kindy management committee runs governance and fundraising activities. The centre maintains links with Newmarket State School for shared activities and transitions, and includes acknowledgements and learning about First Nations culture in its program.

causebase_summary: The Trustee for Invasive Species Solutions Trust, trading as the Centre for Invasive Species Solutions, is an Australian national centre based in the ACT that coordinates collaborative invasive-species research, development and engagement. It hosts and maintains national digital platforms for weed and pest information and tools (weeds.org.au; weedscan.org.au; pestsmart.org.au; feralscan.org.au), coordinates LandSmart Services nationally, develops and disseminates national codes of practice, training and resources, and publishes reports such as the WeedRemeed Impact Report 2024–25. causebase_summary: Accelerated Evolution - The Break Inc. is a volunteer-run not-for-profit based in Caulfield, Melbourne, Victoria, that provides mental health and wellbeing recovery programs. causebase_summary: Araluen Botanic Park Foundation Inc manages Araluen Botanic Park in Roleystone in the Perth Hills, Western Australia. As of August 2026 it maintains 14 hectares of cultivated botanical gardens set within 59 hectares of native West Australian bushland, and manages a significant tree collection and remnant native forest on site. The park hosts public programming including a Tulip Festival, concerts and workshops, operates venue hire for weddings and other events and runs an on‑site café. It recruits and hosts volunteer activities such as a large bulb‑planting day (250,000 bulbs cited) and advertises regular opportunities for visitors to participate. The park is described as open to visitors and supports on‑site wildlife associated with the native bushland.

causebase_summary: Environmental Justice Australia is a public interest legal organisation based in Victoria that works across Australia. It provides legal advice and pro‑bono representation, runs court cases and high‑stakes legal interventions, and conducts advocacy campaigns and legal investigations. The organisation represents communities affected by environmental harm and people with the least power, including providing legal support to Traditional Owners seeking to protect Country and Culture. It pursues matters such as climate litigation, challenges to fossil fuel expansion, and cases to defend forests, rivers and threatened wildlife. The organisation also publishes legal updates and runs public webinars and subscription updates for people who want to follow its work.

causebase_summary: Castlemaine Art Museum is a regional art museum in Castlemaine, Victoria, located on Dja Dja Wurrung / Jaara country. Founded in 1913, it operates a public gallery with free entry Thursday–Sunday and a programme of temporary and scheduled exhibitions. The museum maintains and presents a collection of Australian art, First Nations cultural material and historical artefacts, and runs public events such as openings, artist talks, performances and panel tours. It hosts school group visits, commissions and pays local artists for talks and workshops, and operates a museum shop selling limited-edition artworks. The museum supports its activity through memberships, donations and supporter programs and describes supporter-funded uses including wall labels, artist fees, installation and school group visits.

causebase_summary: Haileybury Rendall School is a co‑educational day, boarding and online school based in Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia. The school runs a compulsory Experiential Outdoor Education programme in remote environments and delivers the VCE curriculum in senior years. causebase_summary: Global Wildlife Fund is an Australian charity that partners with local conservation organisations to support projects to restore wildlife populations and habitats in selected high‑priority areas. It works in Sub‑Saharan Africa (including Matusadona National Park, Zimbabwe), the Andes–Amazon (including Narupa Reserve, Ecuador), New Guinea and the Pacific (Vogelkop Peninsula, Papua, Indonesia) and Asian biodiversity hotspots. The organisation provides funding for wildlife translocations (for example black rhino and sable antelope), helps acquire or expand private non‑profit reserves (for example a 250 ha Narupa Reserve expansion), supports community forest and land‑rights work in Papua, and negotiates project funding agreements while tracking progress and reporting on project outcomes. Directors and founders donate their time to research, assess, support and audit projects, and Australians can make tax‑deductible gifts to support specific projects.

causebase_summary: Biopixel Oceans Foundation Limited is an Australian marine research and education organisation operating on the Great Barrier Reef, Queensland. causebase_summary: Regional Australia Institute (RAI) is a national think tank focused on issues affecting regional Australia. As of August 2026, RAI produces research and data products (for example the Regional Movers Index developed with the Commonwealth Bank, the Regional Labour Markets Update, and the Regionalisation Ambition 2032 progress reports), develops policy and advocacy material (Policy Pulse), and runs events and public programming including the Regions Rising National Summit, Regions Rising WA and member-only Dialogue Day. RAI also offers an executive education Masterclass program for CEOs and executives and delivers partnership projects with external organisations. Its activities are aimed at residents of regional Australia, community, industry and government leaders who use its research and attend its events, and CEOs and executives who enrol in its education programs. It delivers biosecurity awareness training (Green Card Training) recognised by WA government authorities, runs a public conference series (DIG) and other public events, and promotes an ‘Arrive Clean – Leave Clean’ public education campaign. The group publishes guidance and information (Managing Dieback Best Practice Guideline, Treatment News, FAQs) and operates an information referral service (Find an Expert). Its stated stakeholders include government and industry agencies, landholders and land managers, community groups and outdoor recreation users; its work also relates to native plants and regional biodiversity in southern Western Australia. Evidence for these activities comes from the organisation’s website and its 2023 ACNC information statement.

causebase_summary: Newman College is a co‑educational residential college affiliated with the University of Melbourne, located at 887 Swanston Street, Parkville, Victoria. It primarily accepts students enrolled at the University of Melbourne and holds limited places for students in select courses at ACU, Monash and RMIT. The College provides residential accommodation and runs an academic tutorial programme and mentoring (tutorials delivered weekly), administers scholarships and bursaries, and operates a student community service and outreach programme. It also supports sporting teams and inter‑collegiate competitions, music, drama and arts productions and concerts, guest speakers and Scholar’s Presentations, and student retreats (including Camino retreats). Published site metrics include counts for community membership, scholarships and weekly tutorials.

causebase_summary: Angel Gowns Australia Incorporated is a volunteer-run Australian not-for-profit that handcrafts and distributes garments made from donated wedding dresses. causebase_summary: The Water Well Project Limited is an Australian community organisation that runs health education sessions for people from migrant and refugee backgrounds and broader community groups. causebase_summary: The Russian Imperial Order of Saint Michael Archangel is a dynastic order that operates an Australian Division with a registered location in Victoria. causebase_summary: Alcoholics Anonymous, Perth, Western Australia (Aa Service Council For Western Australia) is a local fellowship supporting people who identify a desire to stop drinking. It maintains a staffed office in East Perth with published opening hours (Monday–Friday, 9am–4.30pm) and operates a 24‑hour helpline. The group compiles and publishes meeting lists and a calendar of events (including open and online meetings), provides resources for new members (pamphlets, personal stories, talks and workshops), and publishes or links to AA literature and Serenity magazine. Open meetings are available to anyone interested in AA’s programme of recovery; the site includes specific contact options for fly‑in/fly‑out workers.

causebase_summary: Rossmoyne Kindergarten Association (Inc.) is a community kindergarten in Rossmoyne, City of Canning, Western Australia. It operates two kindergarten classes with a maximum of 20 children per class for children who are four years old by 30 June in the year they attend. The kindergarten occupies purpose-built facilities leased from the City of Canning, with teachers appointed by the Department of Education and management conducted by a parent committee. On-site provision includes an “Enchanted Garden” nature play area with a water pump, sandpits, forts, poultry and small animals, and vegetable patches.
